discovery: The jamming transition as a unifying framework for disordered solids
subfield: Statistical physics of soft and disordered matter
motivation: Liu and Nagel proposed that glasses, granular packings, foams, emulsions and colloids lose or gain rigidity through a common 'jamming' transition. With O'Hern they identified Point J in frictionless sphere packings, a critical point with isostatic contact numbers, power-law scaling of elastic moduli and an excess of soft vibrational modes. This turned a messy many-body problem into a clear physical picture. It explains why amorphous solids differ from crystals in their elasticity, heat transport and plasticity, and it connects microscopic structure to macroscopic mechanics. The framework is now used across physics, chemistry, materials science and biology, from the rheology of dense suspensions to tissue mechanics and the design of tunable mechanical metamaterials. It is a foundational conceptual advance in condensed-matter physics, supported by elegant theory, careful simulation and decisive experiments.
